objective_for_doctor:
Age: 52
Sex: Male
Chief Complaint: I have right side of the chest pain, left side of the chest pain, and right posterior chest wall pain

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’m having bad chest pain—on the right side and also the left side—and pain in the right back of my chest wall. It feels like a knife-stab/sharp pain, and it gets worse when I breathe in (pleuritic). I also feel very short of breath, and my left calf is swollen.

I’m sorry you’re dealing with this. **One question at a time**:

**1) When did the chest pain and shortness of breath start (exact time or how many hours/days ago)?**
It started about **1 hour ago**. The pain came on pretty fast, and the shortness of breath started around the same time.
**2) Do you have any history of blood clots (DVT/PE), recent surgery/immobility, long travel, or are you on estrogen-containing birth control or hormone therapy?**
Yes—I’ve had **deep vein thrombosis** before. I also had **surgery within the last month**, and I had **recent travel to North America**. I’m not on any estrogen hormone therapy/birth control.
**3) How would you describe the shortness of breath—are you able to speak full sentences, and do you feel like you might pass out?**
I’m **very short of breath**. I can still talk, but it’s hard—mostly I can’t comfortably speak in full sentences. And yes, I **felt like I might pass out**; I even **lost consciousness**.
**4) Any symptoms like coughing up blood, fever, or new wheezing?**
No coughing up blood, no fever, and no new wheezing.
**5) Is the chest pain strictly pleuritic (worse with deep breath/cough), and does it change with pressing on your chest wall or moving your torso?**

Yes, it’s **worse with deep breath**—it’s pleuritic. It’s also sharp, and I feel it in the **back of my chest wall** on the right, and it can radiate toward my **left scapula**. I’m not sure about whether pressing on my chest or moving my torso changes it a lot.
**6) Do you have any leg pain or redness on the swollen left calf (tenderness, warmth), and is the swelling new since today or gradual?**
My **left calf is swollen**. I don’t have details to say if it’s warm or red, but it is swollen. I can’t say if it’s new today or gradual—just that it’s there now.
**7) Any recent long period of immobility (bed rest), leg cast/splint, or missed doses of anticoagulation if you’re on blood thinners?**
I had **surgery within the last month**, so I’ve had some reduced movement. I’m not sure about bed rest. I’m not on blood thinners that I missed—no missed doses.
**8) Are you currently taking any anticoagulant (e.g., apixaban, rivaroxaban, warfarin, enoxaparin), and if so what dose?**
I’m **not sure** I’m on an anticoagulant right now, and I can’t give you a dose. I can tell you I don’t think I’ve missed any blood thinner doses.
**9) Do you have any known heart disease, history of atrial fibrillation, or recent palpitations?**
No known heart disease that I’m aware of, no atrial fibrillation. I haven’t noticed palpitations recently.
**10) Any recent infection symptoms (sore throat, cough, runny nose), or is this purely sudden chest pain/shortness of breath?**
No infection symptoms like sore throat, cough, or runny nose. It feels like it came on suddenly with the chest pain and shortness of breath.
**11) Do you have any history of pneumothorax, lung disease (COPD/asthma), or smoking?**
I don’t have a history of pneumothorax, and I don’t have known lung disease like COPD or asthma. I don’t smoke.
**12) On a scale of 0–10, how severe is the chest pain, and is it localized to the right/back area or does it feel like pressure/tightness in the center too?**

The chest pain is **very severe—about 10/10**, and it’s mainly **localized to the right/back chest wall** area. It doesn’t feel like pressure/tightness in the center as much as the sharp pain on the sides and back.
[DDX] Pulmonary embolism, Possible NSTEMI / STEMI, Spontaneous pneumothorax, Acute pulmonary edema, Acute COPD exacerbation / infection
